name: Column grid
description: The column-span system: children of a row declare how many columns they occupy, and optionally which column they start at, per breakpoint range. Width is column-based — you say 'eight of twelve', not '931px'. This is the first of three grid kinds in the system, and the one most layouts should use. Figma calls it Column flex-Grid-8.

breakpointBehavior.behavior: col-sm-1 through col-sm-6 against a 6-column grid. Declared at the top level, so they are the mobile-first base.
col-md-1 through col-md-12 override col-lg-* inside the tablet range, for layouts that need a different stack at tablet.
col-lg-1 through col-lg-12 re-declared at 1280 so they win back over col-md-*.
Inherits the lg spans; HD changes the container, not the column count.

classes.name: col-sm-1
classes.purpose: Span one of six at mobile.

classes.name: col-sm-full
classes.purpose: Span the whole row at mobile, whatever the column count.

classes.name: col-md-6
classes.purpose: Span six of twelve in the tablet range.

classes.name: col-md-full
classes.purpose: Span the whole row in the tablet range.

classes.name: col-lg-8
classes.purpose: Span eight of twelve from 768 up, re-asserted at 1280.

classes.name: col-lg-full
classes.purpose: Span the whole row from 768 up.

classes.name: start-sm-2
classes.purpose: Start at a named column at mobile.

classes.name: start-md-4
classes.purpose: Start at a named column in the tablet range.

classes.name: start-lg-5
classes.purpose: Start at a named column from 768 up — this is how an asymmetric layout is expressed without an empty spacer div.

rules.statement: Column classes only mean anything inside a row; the row is what creates the grid they span.
The mobile range offers a span for every one of its six columns.
The mobile range stops at six. A col-sm-7 would be a span wider than the grid it sits in.
The desktop range offers a span for every one of its twelve columns.
The tablet range offers a span for every one of its twelve columns.
No range offers a thirteenth column.
Explicit column starts exist for the desktop range, so asymmetric layouts need no spacer elements.
Explicit column starts exist for the tablet range.
col-md-* must be declared after col-lg-* inside the 768 range, or the tablet override never wins. Source order is load-bearing here.

check.note: Both families sit in the same @media (min-width: 768px) block with col-md-* second; the 1280 block then re-asserts col-lg-*. Confirmed by reading the stylesheet; a cascade check would need a real CSS cascade model.

rules.statement: The gutter between columns is the same 8px Figma's layout guide uses.

decisions.question: row-span-* utilities exist for all three ranges but only do anything inside a bento grid, where rows have a fixed height. Should they move to the bento contract or stay general?
decisions.evidence: In a plain .row the rows are content-sized, so grid-row: span 2 has no predictable effect. They are documented under bento-grid for now.

visualize.note: Each row is a real .row with real col-lg-* children, so what you see is the stylesheet, not a drawing of it.
